mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 350 or 400 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a C350 or C400 petrol typically costs between £600 and £5,500 depending on the engine code and condition. Used M272 units start from £600-£1,500, reconditioned from £1,800-£3,200, and fully rebuilt M276 biturbo engines from £2,800-£5,500. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: What is the balance shaft failure on the M272 V6 engine in the C350?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early M272 engines (serial numbers below 2729..30 468993, 2004-2008) suffer from balance shaft sprocket wear due to soft metal being used in the manufacturing process of the timing gear. This causes the timing to be thrown off, triggering fault codes P0016/P0017. Symptoms include a check engine light, rough idle, and potential engine damage if not addressed. Repair costs at a specialist are approximately £2,200-£3,500 for balance shaft and timing chain replacement.

mainEntity.name: Does the C-Class 350 or 400 petrol have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the M272 and M276 engines use timing chains, not belts. The M272 uses a 90° V-angle with a balance shaft. The M276 uses a 60° V-angle which reduces vibrations to such an extent that a balance shaft is no longer necessary. However, the M272 is known for balance shaft sprocket wear, and the M276 is known for camshaft adjuster rattle and timing chain tensioner wear.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a C-Class 350 or 400 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M272-equipped models (W204 C350, 2008-2011), the most common symptom is a check engine light with codes P0016/P0017, rough idle, and potential engine damage from balance shaft wear. On M276-equipped models (W204 C350 facelift, W205 C400, 2011-2017), symptoms include a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start (camshaft adjuster or timing chain tensioner), reduced power or intermittent limp mode, delayed boost response, and wastegate rattle.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 350 or 400 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W204 C350 is typically worth £3,000-£8,000 - a rebuilt M272 engine (£2,200-£4,200) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W205 C400 is worth £8,000-£18,000 - a rebuilt M276 biturbo engine (£2,800-£5,500) is usually well within the car's value. For the M272, if caught early, a balance shaft replacement is more economical than a full engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M272 and M276 engines in the C350?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272 is a 3.5-litre naturally aspirated 90° V6 used in the W204 C350 (2008-2011), producing 272 hp. The M276 is a 3.5-litre 60° V6 with direct injection used in the W204 C350 facelift (2011-2014), producing 306 hp. The M276's 60° V-angle reduces vibrations to such an extent that a balance shaft is no longer necessary. The M276 also features direct injection (CGI) for improved efficiency and power. The M276.823 is a 3.0-litre biturbo variant used in the C400 (2014-2017), producing 333 hp.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 350 / 400 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C350 and C400 petrol badges represent the V6-powered performance offerings across two generations of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class. The C350 arrived with the W204 generation in 2008, powered by the naturally aspirated M272 3.5-litre V6. In 2011, the C350 received the updated M276 3.5-litre V6 with direct injection. The C400 badge was introduced with the W205 generation in 2014, featuring the M276 3.0-litre V6 biturbo engine - a significant leap forward in performance and efficiency.

milestones.description: M272.960, 3.5L V6 petrol, 272 hp (200 kW) - W204 C350 launch; 90° V-angle, naturally aspirated; 350 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 6.1 seconds
M272.961, 3.5L V6 petrol, 272 hp - W204 C350 4MATIC variant
M276.957, 3.5L V6 petrol, 306 hp (225 kW) - W204 C350 facelift; 60° V-angle, direct injection; 370 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 5.9 seconds
M276.823, 3.0L V6 biturbo petrol, 333 hp (245 kW) - W205 C400 launch; 60° V-angle, twin-turbocharged; 480 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 5.1 seconds; 4MATIC standard
C400 badge discontinued; replaced by C43 AMG (M276.823 with 367 hp)

problems.h4: M272 Balance Shaft Sprocket Wear - The W204 C350 V6's Critical Weakness
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 350 petrol (M272.960 and M272.961, W204, 2008-2011)
problems.rootCause: The balance shaft in early M272 V6 engines was known to have problems due to soft metal being used in the manufacturing process of the timing gear. M272 engines with serial numbers below 2729..30 468993 are affected. Since the balance shaft is part of the timing components, a worn or damaged balance shaft can throw timing off, causing poor engine performance or, in extreme cases, cylinder head damage.

repairOptions.longevity: Required if timing has jumped or engine damage has occurred

For vehicles under £4,000, a balance shaft replacement (£2,200-£3,500) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M272 with warranty (£3,200-£5,500) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If your W204 C350 V6 throws codes P0016/P0017 and you have an early M272 engine (serial below 2729..30 468993), the balance shaft sprocket is almost certainly the cause. problems.group: M276 Camshaft Adjuster & Timing Chain Tensioner Rattle
problems.h4: M276 Camshaft Adjuster & Timing Chain Tensioner Rattle - Cold Start Noise in the C350 / C400
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 350 and 400 petrol (M276.957 and M276.823, W204 and W205, 2011-2017)
problems.rootCause: The M276 engine suffers from camshaft adjuster failure and timing chain tensioner wear. Cold start rattle is a common symptom. Mercedes has a service bulletin (LI05.10-P-056435) on this for M276/M278 engines. The problem originates from secondary timing chains, and the recommended fix is to install check valves and chain tensioners. M276 has secondary tensioner oil feed issues - when parked, the pressure/oil drains back out and causes it to rattle for a few seconds until oil pressure returns.

repairOptions.tier: Timing Chain Tensioner & Check Valve Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioners and install check valves
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; prevents camshaft adjuster damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed camshaft adjuster(s), timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if adjuster has failed and is causing performance issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new camshaft adjusters, tensioners and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value on higher-mileage cars

problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start - particularly on M276-equipped models - have the timing chain tensioners and camshaft adjusters inspected immediately. A £700-£1,200 specialist tensioner and check valve replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the camshaft adjusters fail, replacement costs approach rebuild territory.

problems.h4: M276 Biturbo Turbocharger & Wastegate Issues - Boost Loss and Reduced Power (C400)
problems.rootCause: The M276 biturbo engine can suffer from wastegate rattle, linkage wear and underboost complaints. Common customer complaints include reduced power, intermittent limp mode, poor acceleration, delayed boost response, a check engine light, or a rattle from the turbocharger area.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Repair or replace wastegate linkage and actuator
Replace or rebuild turbocharger, oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo has failed or wastegate is seized

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new turbocharger components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your C400 experiences reduced power or a rattle from the engine bay, have the turbocharger and wastegate system inspected. A £500-£900 wastegate repair is significantly cheaper than a £1,800 turbo replacement. Regular oil changes and using high-quality fuel can help extend turbo life.
